test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following CANNOT be accepted by the general public in India regarding GHI?

options.text: The GHI report takes India’s data from our own National Family Health Survey.
One of the two organisations that prepare GHI is from Ireland.
If our children are not tall enough or do not weigh enough, it is an indicator of national hunger.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage indicates that the criteria used by the GHI report, such as child stunting and child wasting rates, are debatable in relation **to the idea of national hunger.**
 
• Many people might not accept that inadequate** height or weight of children directly correlates with national hung**er.
 
• Options 1, 2, and 3 are stated facts in the passage that the general public can likely accept:
 
 
• 19% of Indian children are wasted.
 
• The GHI report takes India's data from the National Family Health Survey.
 
• One of the two organisations that prepare GHI is from Ireland.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**, as it is the least likely to be accepted without questioning.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "19% of Indian children are wasted." - This is a fact based on the National Family Health Survey data.
 
• **Option 2:** "The GHI report takes India’s data from our own National Family Health Survey." - This is also a fact mentioned in the passage.
 
• **Option 3:** "One of the two organisations that prepare GHI is from Ireland." - This is another factual statement made in the passage.
